/-!
# Sequences with Large Gaps

*References:*
 - [Wa01] Wang, Yuefei. "On the Fatou set of an entire function with gaps." Tohoku Mathematical
    Journal, Second Series 53.1 (2001): 163-170.
-/

open Set Filter Topology
open scoped Finset

/-- A sequence of natural numbers `n₀ < n₁ < ...` is said to have Fabry gaps if `nₖ / k → ∞`.
This is the terminology adopted in [Wa01] and some other sources. -/
def HasFabryGaps (n : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := StrictMono n ∧ Tendsto (fun k => n k / (k : ℝ)) atTop atTop

/-- A sequence of natural numbers `n₀ < n₁ < ...` is said to have Fejér gaps if `∑' 1 / nₖ < ∞`.
This is the terminology adopted in [Wa01] and some other sources. -/
def HasFejerGaps (n : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := StrictMono n ∧ Summable (fun k => (n k : ℝ)⁻¹)

theorem HasFejerGaps.hasFabryGaps {f : ℕ → ℕ} (hf : HasFejerGaps f) : HasFabryGaps f := by
  refine ⟨hf.1, tendsto_atTop_mono'
    (f₁ := (· / 2) ∘ (·⁻¹) ∘ (∑' n : Set.Ici ·, (f n : ℝ)⁻¹) ∘ (· / 2)) _ ?_ <|
      (tendsto_div_const_atTop_of_pos (two_pos (α := ℝ))).2 <| tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero.comp <|
        .comp (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff.2 ⟨?_, ?_⟩) <| Nat.tendsto_div_const_atTop two_ne_zero⟩
  · filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop 1] with N hN
    simp only [Function.comp_apply, Nat.ofNat_pos, div_le_iff₀]
    have : 0 < f N := (hf.1 hN).bot_lt
    refine inv_le_of_inv_le₀ (by positivity) ?_
    calc
      (f N / N * 2 : ℝ)⁻¹
        = N / 2 * (f N : ℝ)⁻¹ := by grind
      _ ≤ #(.Ico (N / 2) N) • (f N : ℝ)⁻¹ := by simp; gcongr; simp [div_le_iff₀]; norm_cast; omega
      _ ≤ ∑ n ∈ .Ico (N / 2) N, (f n : ℝ)⁻¹ := Finset.card_nsmul_le_sum _ _ _ fun n hn ↦ by
        rw [Finset.mem_Ico] at hn
        have : 0 < f n := (hf.1 <| show 0 < n by omega).bot_lt
        grw [(hf.1 hn.2).le]
      _ ≤ ∑' n : Ici (N / 2), (f n : ℝ)⁻¹ :=
        hf.2.sum_le_tsum_set (by simp [Ico_subset_Ici_self]) (by simp)
  · exact hf.2.tendsto_tsum_zero (fun b ↦ by simpa using eventually_gt_atTop b)
  · filter_upwards [eventually_gt_atTop 0] with N hN
    refine (hf.2.comp_injective Subtype.val_injective).tsum_pos (by simp) ⟨N, by simp⟩ ?_
    simpa using (hf.1 hN).bot_lt

findings.description: An additional defect in the adjacent Kövari variant in FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/516.lean: unlike the reviewed gap predicates, its growth hypothesis does not require StrictMono n. Repeated exponents can therefore cancel despite every coefficient being nonzero. Explicitly, take n(2j) = n(2j+1) = (2j+2)^4 and a(k) = (-1)^k / (n(k)!). These satisfy the stated bound with c = 1, and the series converges absolutely everywhere but sums to the zero function. Consequently the stated limsup is 0, not 1. All hypotheses and the failure of the conclusion were proved in /workspace/review/kovari_counterexample.lean, with no sorry dependencies. This is not a defect in HasGaps.lean itself or in its four direct predicate uses.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/516 states Kövari's gap-series result with n_k > k(log k)^(2+c), c > 0, and conclusion limsup log m(r)/log M(r) = 1. The exponents in this gap-series setting enumerate distinct Taylor degrees; the convention is explicit in Fuchs, 'Proof of a conjecture of G. Pólya concerning gap series', §1, p. 661: 'an increasing sequence of nonnegative integers' (https://doi.org/10.1215/ijm/1255645102). Both reviewed gap predicates correctly enforce this convention with StrictMono.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hypothesis `(hn_mono : StrictMono n)` to Erdos516.erdos_516.variants.limsup_ratio_eq_one, retaining its existing growth and nonzero-coefficient hypotheses.

reformulations.difference: Wang's reciprocal-series condition starts at k = 1, whereas Lean uses real-valued Summable over all natural indices, including a possibly zero first exponent.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: StrictMono n implies n(k) > 0 for every k > 0. Removing the first real reciprocal term does not change summability, even when n(0) = 0 and Lean assigns its reciprocal the value zero. All reciprocal terms are nonnegative, so unconditional Summable is equivalent to convergence of the ordinary partial sums to a finite real value. Both the first-term deletion equivalence and the partial-sum characterization were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean includes k = 0 in the quotient and uses Tendsto atTop atTop on ℝ; the sources use an asymptotic ratio, usually with positive indexing.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The value of the quotient at k = 0 cannot affect a limit at infinity. The Lean condition is exactly eventual exceedance of every real bound. Reindexing the first term from index zero to index one replaces n(k)/k by n(k)/(k+1); for k ≥ 1 the latter lies between half the former and the former, so divergence to positive infinity is equivalent. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical defect was found in either definition or in HasFejerGaps.hasFabryGaps, and all four direct uses of these predicates in problems 516 and 517 have the intended gap semantics. The single finding concerns an adjacent variant inspected during the use-site review, not an inherited library defect. Constant and linear sequences were proved to fail both predicates; square exponents were proved to satisfy both, including the zero initial exponent. No Mathlib duplicate or conflicting homonym was found. scratch.lean, check_uses.lean, and kovari_counterexample.lean compile successfully. The counterexample and the library implication depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Direct website requests were blocked, so the cited paper text and Erdős pages were read through r.jina.ai. Kövari's original scanned text was unavailable, but its statement was checked against the Erdős LaTeX source and the formal counterexample. No repository files were edited; the reviewed file's checksum matches the specified commit.
